paragraphs.title: Love of the Lord and Remembering His Deeds

easy.question: What does the people command toward the Lord?
answers: To love the Lord and keep His commandments
To build Him a palace
To leave immediately for the wilderness
easy.explanation: Verse 1 commands them to love the Lord and keep His charge, statutes, judgments, and commandments.

easy.question: Who had not known or seen the greatness and deeds of the Lord?
answers: Pharaoh and his servants
The younger Israelites
Dathan and Abiram
easy.explanation: Moses says he is speaking to the adults, not to their children, who had not seen the Lord's past deeds.

easy.question: What did the Lord do to the Egyptians who pursued the Israelites?
answers: He led them into the wilderness
He gave them a new land
He drowned and destroyed them in the Red Sea
easy.explanation: The Lord caused the Red Sea to overwhelm the Egyptians pursuing Israel and destroyed them.

medium.question: Which event occurred after the signs in Egypt and before the deeds in the wilderness?
answers: The Lord destroyed the Egyptian army in the Red Sea
The earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram
The Israelites entered the land
medium.explanation: The passage describes the deeds in Egypt, then the Red Sea, and afterward the events in the wilderness.

medium.question: What does the phrase "the chastisement of the Lord your God" refer to?
answers: A song of praise
The instruction or discipline through which people learn
A valuable gift
medium.explanation: In this context, chastisement means instruction or discipline learned through the Lord's mighty deeds.

medium.question: Why does the passage emphasize that the Israelites themselves saw the Lord's deeds?
answers: To say that they were kings of Egypt
To explain that they were not in the wilderness
To strengthen their duty to remember and obey the Lord
medium.explanation: Those who personally witnessed the Lord's deeds had a special responsibility to remember them and live accordingly.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the Israelites Moses is addressing and their children?
answers: The parents saw the Lord's deeds themselves, but the children did not
The parents were in Egypt, while the children were at the Red Sea
The parents did not know the Lord, but the children did
challenge.explanation: Moses bases his appeal on personal testimony: the older Israelites saw the great deeds, unlike their children.

challenge.question: What does the phrase "unto this day" indicate about the destruction of the Egyptians?
answers: The Egyptians immediately returned home
The event remained an established fact and a continuing memory
The event happened only after Israel entered the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the event and its memory still stand at the time Moses is speaking.

challenge.question: Which detail especially emphasizes the extent of Dathan and Abiram's punishment?
answers: That they were sons of Eliab
That the event occurred in the wilderness
That the earth swallowed them, their households, and all their possessions
challenge.explanation: The passage describes not only the men being swallowed but also their households, tents, and possessions.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the Israelites Moses is addressing and their children?
answers: The parents saw the Lord's deeds themselves, but the children did not
The parents were in Egypt, while the children were at the Red Sea
The parents did not know the Lord, but the children did
questions.explanation: Moses bases his appeal on personal testimony: the older Israelites saw the great deeds, unlike their children.

questions.question: What does the phrase "unto this day" indicate about the destruction of the Egyptians?
answers: The Egyptians immediately returned home
The event remained an established fact and a continuing memory
The event happened only after Israel entered the land
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the event and its memory still stand at the time Moses is speaking.

questions.question: Which detail especially emphasizes the extent of Dathan and Abiram's punishment?
answers: That they were sons of Eliab
That the event occurred in the wilderness
That the earth swallowed them, their households, and all their possessions
questions.explanation: The passage describes not only the men being swallowed but also their households, tents, and possessions.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the Commandments and the Promised Land

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to keep?
answers: All the commandments
Only the Sabbath commandment
The laws of Egypt
easy.explanation: Verse 8 commands them to keep all the commandments.

easy.question: What will happen if the Israelites keep the commandments?
answers: They will return to Egypt
They will become strong and possess the land
They will no longer need to work
easy.explanation: Keeping the commandments will enable them to become strong, enter the land, and possess it.

easy.question: What kind of land is the land they are entering?
answers: A land of mountains only
A land without water
A land of hills and valleys
easy.explanation: The passage describes it as a land of hills and valleys.

medium.question: What is the connection between keeping the commandments and living in the land?
answers: Keeping the commandments is connected with becoming strong and possessing the land
Keeping the commandments causes them to leave the land
There is no connection between the commandments and the land
medium.explanation: The passage presents obedience as leading to strength and possession of the land.

medium.question: What does the Lord's care for the land show?
answers: He commands Israel to leave it
He watches over it and cares for it
He is searching for another land
medium.explanation: The Lord's eyes are always upon the land, showing that He watches over and cares for it.

medium.question: What is the main difference between Egypt and the land the Israelites are entering?
answers: Nothing is planted in Egypt
The new land has no hills or valleys
Egypt is watered by human labor, while the new land receives water from heaven
medium.explanation: Egypt is watered by human effort, whereas the new land drinks the rain of heaven.

challenge.question: Why does describing the land as dependent on rain reinforce the idea that the Lord watches over it?
answers: Because the rain needed for farming depends on the Lord's care
Because no planting is needed there
Because all the water comes from the Nile
challenge.explanation: The land receives its water from heaven, making the Lord's continual care especially significant.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the comparison with watering a garden in Egypt?
answers: Farming in Israel is always easier
In Egypt people can water the land themselves, while Israel depends more on rain
The Israelites learned to water crops only with their feet
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts human irrigation in Egypt with dependence on rainfall in the promised land.

challenge.question: What does "from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year" mean?
answers: Only at the beginning of the year
Only during the harvest
Throughout the entire year
challenge.explanation: The phrase covers the complete year and emphasizes that the Lord's care is continuous.

questions.question: Why does describing the land as dependent on rain reinforce the idea that the Lord watches over it?
answers: Because the rain needed for farming depends on the Lord's care
Because no planting is needed there
Because all the water comes from the Nile
questions.explanation: The land receives its water from heaven, making the Lord's continual care especially significant.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the comparison with watering a garden in Egypt?
answers: Farming in Israel is always easier
In Egypt people can water the land themselves, while Israel depends more on rain
The Israelites learned to water crops only with their feet
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts human irrigation in Egypt with dependence on rainfall in the promised land.

questions.question: What does "from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year" mean?
answers: Only at the beginning of the year
Only during the harvest
Throughout the entire year
questions.explanation: The phrase covers the complete year and emphasizes that the Lord's care is continuous.

paragraphs.title: Rainfall Blessing and Warning Against Idolatry

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to do in verse 13?
answers: To love the Lord and serve Him with all their heart and soul
To build new cities
To go to war
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to love the Lord and serve Him with all their heart and soul.

easy.question: What will the Lord give the land if the Israelites obey His commandments?
answers: Snow all year
Rain in its proper season
New rivers
easy.explanation: The Lord promises to give the land rain at the proper time.

easy.question: What does Moses warn the Israelites against in verse 16?
answers: Working in the fields
Eating the produce of the land
Serving other gods and worshiping them
easy.explanation: The verse warns them not to turn aside and serve other gods.

medium.question: What is the connection between obedience and the abundance described in verses 13–15?
answers: Obedience brings rain, crops, food, and satisfaction
Obedience stops the rain
Obedience requires leaving the land
medium.explanation: When Israel loves and serves the Lord, He gives rain, crops, grass for livestock, and food in abundance.

medium.question: What does "the latter rain" mean in the phrase "the first rain and the latter rain"?
answers: A strong wind
Rain that falls later in the season
The harvest that has been gathered
medium.explanation: The latter rain is the later rainfall that comes toward the end of the rainy season.

medium.question: What may happen if the Israelites serve other gods?
answers: The land will produce more crops
The Israelites will receive double rain
The rain will stop and the land will not yield its produce
medium.explanation: The passage says that idolatry will anger the Lord, causing the heavens to close and the harvest to fail.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the repeated wording "hearken diligently"?
answers: Serious attention and obedience to the commandments
A ban on speaking during prayer
A command to listen only once
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes not merely hearing but listening attentively and obeying.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the blessing includes both people and animals?
answers: The mention of idolatry
Grass in the fields for livestock and food until people are full
The closing of the heavens
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions grass for livestock as well as food and satisfaction for people.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between verses 13–15 and verses 16–17?
answers: The difference between city and countryside
The difference between summer and winter
Faithfulness brings abundance, while idolatry brings drought and loss
challenge.explanation: The verses present two opposite paths: obedience brings rain and crops, while idolatry brings drought and loss of the land.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the repeated wording "hearken diligently"?
answers: Serious attention and obedience to the commandments
A ban on speaking during prayer
A command to listen only once
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes not merely hearing but listening attentively and obeying.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the blessing includes both people and animals?
answers: The mention of idolatry
Grass in the fields for livestock and food until people are full
The closing of the heavens
questions.explanation: The passage mentions grass for livestock as well as food and satisfaction for people.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between verses 13–15 and verses 16–17?
answers: The difference between city and countryside
The difference between summer and winter
Faithfulness brings abundance, while idolatry brings drought and loss
questions.explanation: The verses present two opposite paths: obedience brings rain and crops, while idolatry brings drought and loss of the land.

paragraphs.title: The Commandments in the Heart and Family Life

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to do with these words?
answers: To lay them up in their hearts and souls
To hide them in their houses
To give them only to the king
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to lay the words up in their hearts and souls.

easy.question: Whom are they commanded to teach?
answers: Their neighbors
Their children
The priests alone
easy.explanation: The passage says, "Ye shall teach them your children."

easy.question: Where are they commanded to write the words?
answers: On trees in the wilderness
In the king's book
On the doorposts of the house and on the gates
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to write the words on their doorposts and gates.

medium.question: What is the central sequence of actions in these verses?
answers: Lay up the words in the heart, teach the children, and write them on the doorposts
Build a house, set out on a journey, and teach the children
Write them on the gates, forget them, and then learn them
medium.explanation: The passage first commands inward devotion, then teaching the children, and finally visible writing.

medium.question: What does the phrase "as frontlets between your eyes" indicate?
answers: Gates
Visible signs or reminders
Foods
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a visible sign or reminder worn in a prominent place.

medium.question: What result does the passage promise to those who keep these words?
answers: Immediate wealth
Victory in every war
Long life in the land
medium.explanation: Verse 21 says that the days of the people and their children will be multiplied in the land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from "when thou sittest in thine house...when thou risest up"?
answers: The words should be remembered and taught throughout daily life
They may be discussed only at home
They should be studied only before bed
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions different daily activities to show that the words should accompany people throughout life.

challenge.question: What does the connection between the heart and soul and the signs and writing emphasize?
answers: The commandments are only external signs
The words must be internalized and expressed through visible actions
The heart and soul are physical places for writing
challenge.explanation: The passage combines inward commitment with outward signs and behavior.

challenge.question: What does the comparison "as the days of heaven upon the earth" mean?
answers: Life will be very short
The land will disappear
The days will continue for a long and stable time
challenge.explanation: The comparison expresses a promise of enduring life in the land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from "when thou sittest in thine house...when thou risest up"?
answers: The words should be remembered and taught throughout daily life
They may be discussed only at home
They should be studied only before bed
questions.explanation: The passage mentions different daily activities to show that the words should accompany people throughout life.

questions.question: What does the connection between the heart and soul and the signs and writing emphasize?
answers: The commandments are only external signs
The words must be internalized and expressed through visible actions
The heart and soul are physical places for writing
questions.explanation: The passage combines inward commitment with outward signs and behavior.

questions.question: What does the comparison "as the days of heaven upon the earth" mean?
answers: Life will be very short
The land will disappear
The days will continue for a long and stable time
questions.explanation: The comparison expresses a promise of enduring life in the land.

paragraphs.title: Clinging to the Lord and Possessing the Land

easy.question: What does Moses command the Israelites to do?
answers: To keep all the commandments, love the Lord, and walk in His ways
To build cities in every land
To fight without the Lord's help
easy.explanation: Verse 22 commands them to keep the commandments, love the Lord, walk in His ways, and cling to Him.

easy.question: What does the Lord promise to do to the nations living in the land?
answers: Make them slaves
Drive them out before Israel
Leave them in place
easy.explanation: Verse 23 says that the Lord will drive all those nations out before Israel.

easy.question: What will the Lord place upon the peoples throughout the land?
answers: Wealth alone
Only completed houses
Fear and dread of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 25 says that the Lord will place Israel's fear and dread upon the land.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Israel keeps the commandments, the Lord drives out the nations, and Israel possesses the land
Israel possesses the land and then begins keeping the commandments
The nations win, and only afterward does the Lord give Israel the land
medium.explanation: The passage presents obedience first, the Lord's action against the nations second, and possession of the land afterward.

medium.question: What does "the Lord shall drive out all these nations" mean?
answers: He will give the nations an inheritance
He will remove the nations from the land
He will ask the nations for advice
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means that the Lord will remove or dispossess the nations.

medium.question: What boundaries are given for the land Israel will possess?
answers: From the Mediterranean Sea to Egypt only
Only around Jerusalem
From the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates River and the utmost sea
medium.explanation: Verse 24 gives a broad territory extending from the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates and the farthest sea.

challenge.question: What does "Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours" emphasize?
answers: The places where Israel walks will become part of the land given to them
Only the place where Moses walked will be given to Israel
The whole world will be given to Israel without limits
challenge.explanation: The phrase connects Israel's occupation of the land with possessing it within the stated boundaries.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between verses 22 and 23?
answers: The land will be given regardless of Israel's behavior
Faithfulness to the Lord is presented as preceding victory and possession of the land
The nations command Israel to keep the commandments
challenge.explanation: Verse 22 presents obedience and devotion to the Lord before verse 23 describes the nations being driven out.

challenge.question: What does "as he hath said unto you" mean at the end of verse 25?
answers: The people must ask the nations what to do
The promise was spoken only after entering the land
The event fulfills an earlier promise made to Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to what the Lord had already said and promised to Israel.

questions.question: What does "Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours" emphasize?
answers: The places where Israel walks will become part of the land given to them
Only the place where Moses walked will be given to Israel
The whole world will be given to Israel without limits
questions.explanation: The phrase connects Israel's occupation of the land with possessing it within the stated boundaries.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between verses 22 and 23?
answers: The land will be given regardless of Israel's behavior
Faithfulness to the Lord is presented as preceding victory and possession of the land
The nations command Israel to keep the commandments
questions.explanation: Verse 22 presents obedience and devotion to the Lord before verse 23 describes the nations being driven out.

questions.question: What does "as he hath said unto you" mean at the end of verse 25?
answers: The people must ask the nations what to do
The promise was spoken only after entering the land
The event fulfills an earlier promise made to Israel
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to what the Lord had already said and promised to Israel.

paragraphs.title: Blessing and Curse Before the Choice

easy.question: What does the Lord set before the people?
answers: A blessing and a curse
War and peace
Rain and drought
easy.explanation: Verse 26 says that the Lord sets a blessing and a curse before the people.

easy.question: When will the blessing come?
answers: When the people win a war
When the people obey the Lord's commandments
When the people build a city
easy.explanation: The passage connects the blessing with obeying the Lord's commandments.

easy.question: What leads to the curse according to these verses?
answers: Turning away from the commanded way and following other gods
Keeping the commandments
Listening to Moses
easy.explanation: The curse comes when the people do not obey, turn aside from the way, and follow other gods.

medium.question: What is the connection between obeying the commandments and the blessing?
answers: Obedience is the condition for receiving the blessing
Obedience cancels the blessing
There is no connection
medium.explanation: Verse 27 presents the blessing as the result of obeying the Lord's commandments.

medium.question: What does "turn aside out of the way" mean in context?
answers: To become stronger on the way
To stray or turn away
To walk faster
medium.explanation: The phrase describes turning away from the right path.

medium.question: What sequence leads to the curse?
answers: Obedience, followed by blessing
Blessing, followed by leaving the way
Disobedience, turning aside, and following other gods
medium.explanation: Verse 28 describes failure to obey, turning from the commanded way, and following other gods.

challenge.question: Why is the word "this day" emphasized in these verses?
answers: To emphasize that the command and choice stand before the people now
To identify a particular festival
To say that the commandments last only one day
challenge.explanation: The repeated reference to this day stresses that the people must respond in the present.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from placing the blessing and curse side by side?
answers: They are given regardless of behavior
The people's behavior leads to the corresponding result
The curse is more important than the blessing
challenge.explanation: The verses clearly connect obedience with blessing and disobedience with curse.

challenge.question: What does "which ye have not known" mean regarding other gods?
answers: The people had already served them
The people had studied them thoroughly
They are foreign gods whom the people did not know
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that these are strange gods outside the way Israel had been taught.

questions.question: Why is the word "this day" emphasized in these verses?
answers: To emphasize that the command and choice stand before the people now
To identify a particular festival
To say that the commandments last only one day
questions.explanation: The repeated reference to this day stresses that the people must respond in the present.

questions.question: What can be inferred from placing the blessing and curse side by side?
answers: They are given regardless of behavior

questions.explanation: The verses clearly connect obedience with blessing and disobedience with curse.

answers: The people had already served them

questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that these are strange gods outside the way Israel had been taught.

easy.question: On which mountain will the blessing be placed?
answers: Mount Gerizim
Mount Ebal
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The passage says, "Thou shalt put the blessing upon mount Gerizim."

easy.question: What will happen when the Lord brings Israel into the land?
answers: They will return to Egypt
They will place the blessing and curse on the mountains
They will build the tabernacle in the wilderness
easy.explanation: After entering the land, the blessing will be placed on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

easy.question: On which mountain will the curse be placed?
answers: Mount Gerizim
Mount Carmel
Mount Ebal
easy.explanation: The passage specifically names Mount Ebal as the mountain of the curse.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Entering the land, followed by placing the blessing and curse on the mountains
Placing the blessing and curse, followed by leaving Egypt
Building cities, followed by crossing the Red Sea
medium.explanation: First the Lord brings Israel into the land; afterward the blessing and curse are placed on the two mountains.

medium.question: What does "to possess it" mean in the phrase "the land whither thou goest to possess it"?
answers: To leave it
To receive it as an inheritance
To hide in it
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to entering the land in order to receive and hold it as an inheritance.

medium.question: Which details describe the location of the mountains?
answers: Beyond Jordan, in the land of Canaan, opposite Gilgal
In the wilderness of Sinai, near the Red Sea
In Egypt, opposite Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Verse 30 places them beyond Jordan, in Canaan, opposite Gilgal, near the plains of Moreh.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from placing the blessing and curse on two different mountains?
answers: There is no difference between blessing and curse
The people face a choice with different consequences for their actions
The mountains themselves are gods
challenge.explanation: The separation of the two mountains emphasizes choice and the different results of obedience and disobedience.

challenge.question: Which easily overlooked detail appears in the description of the location?
answers: The mountains are in the wilderness of Sinai
They are opposite Gilgal
They are inside Egypt
challenge.explanation: The location is explicitly described as being opposite Gilgal.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between verses 29 and 30?
answers: Verse 29 gives the mountains' role, and verse 30 describes their location
Verse 29 tells of the exodus, and verse 30 tells of building the tabernacle
Verse 29 describes a war, and verse 30 describes a king
challenge.explanation: Verse 29 states what will be placed on each mountain, while verse 30 adds geographical details.

questions.question: What can be inferred from placing the blessing and curse on two different mountains?
answers: There is no difference between blessing and curse
The people face a choice with different consequences for their actions
The mountains themselves are gods
questions.explanation: The separation of the two mountains emphasizes choice and the different results of obedience and disobedience.

questions.question: Which easily overlooked detail appears in the description of the location?
answers: The mountains are in the wilderness of Sinai
They are opposite Gilgal
They are inside Egypt
questions.explanation: The location is explicitly described as being opposite Gilgal.

questions.question: What is the relationship between verses 29 and 30?
answers: Verse 29 gives the mountains' role, and verse 30 describes their location

paragraphs.title: Crossing the Jordan and Possessing the Land

easy.question: What are the Israelites about to cross?
answers: The Jordan
The wilderness
The sea
easy.explanation: The verse says, "Ye shall pass over Jordan."

easy.question: Why will the Israelites cross the Jordan?
answers: To return to Egypt
To possess the land
To build the tabernacle
easy.explanation: They will cross the Jordan in order to enter and possess the land.

easy.question: What will the Israelites do after possessing the land?
answers: Leave it
Cross the sea
Dwell in it
easy.explanation: The verse says that they will possess the land and dwell therein.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the verse?
answers: Cross the Jordan, possess the land, and dwell in it
Dwell in the land, cross the Jordan, and possess it
Possess the land, leave it, and cross the Jordan
medium.explanation: The verse presents crossing the Jordan, possessing the land, and then dwelling in it.

medium.question: What does "to possess the land" mean in context?
answers: To see the land
To receive ownership of it and hold it
To pass by the land
medium.explanation: The context shows that Israel will receive and hold the land, then dwell in it.

medium.question: What is the connection between the Lord giving the land and Israel dwelling in it?
answers: Because the Lord gives it, Israel will possess it and dwell in it
They will dwell there without crossing the Jordan
They receive the land in order to leave it
medium.explanation: The verse presents the Lord's gift of the land as the basis for Israel's possession and dwelling there.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the plural words "ye" and "you"?
answers: The words are addressed to all the Israelites
The words are addressed to one person
The words are addressed only to priests
challenge.explanation: The plural forms show that the verse addresses the Israelite people as a whole.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by "which the Lord your God giveth you"?
answers: The land was purchased with their money
The land is given to them by the Lord
The land belongs to a foreign king
challenge.explanation: The verse directly attributes the giving of the land to the Lord.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that dwelling in the land follows possessing it?
answers: The word "for"
The word "Jordan"
The words "ye shall possess it, and dwell therein"
challenge.explanation: The two actions occur in order: first possessing the land, then dwelling in it.

The words are addressed only to priests

The word "Jordan"

easy.question: What does the verse command the people to do?
answers: To observe and do all the statutes and judgments
To choose only some of the laws
To teach the laws to other nations
easy.explanation: The verse commands the people to observe and do all the statutes and judgments.

easy.question: Who gives the statutes and judgments according to the verse?
answers: The people
The speaker, who says "I"
The kings
easy.explanation: The phrase "which I set before you" identifies the speaker as the one giving the laws.

easy.question: When are the statutes and judgments set before the people?
answers: Yesterday
In the future
Today
easy.explanation: The verse ends with "which I set before you this day."

medium.question: What can be understood from the command "observe to do"?
answers: The people must both keep the laws in mind and carry them out
It is enough to hear the laws
Only one judgment must be obeyed
medium.explanation: The command joins observing with doing, requiring both commitment and action.

medium.question: Why does the verse say "all the statutes and judgments"?
answers: To permit choosing only the easy ones
To emphasize that every instruction must be obeyed
To speak only about legal matters
medium.explanation: The word "all" shows that the command includes the entire body of statutes and judgments.

medium.question: What does "set before you" mean in context?
answers: Behind you
Inside your house
Placed in front of you
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the laws are presented before the people at that time.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word "this day" at the end of the verse?
answers: The command is already relevant when it is spoken
The command will begin only many years later
The command refers only to the past
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the laws are given and required in the present.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that the commandments are not merely to be known?
answers: The phrase "before you"
The phrase "observe to do"
The phrase "this day"
challenge.explanation: "Observe to do" requires not only knowing or remembering but also putting the commandments into practice.

challenge.question: What does the word "all" show about the scope of the command?
answers: It applies only to the judgments
It applies only to the easier laws
It includes every statute and judgment
challenge.explanation: The word "all" makes clear that none of the instructions is excluded.

answers: The command is already relevant when it is spoken
The command will begin only many years later
The command refers only to the past
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the laws are given and required in the present.

questions.question: Which wording shows that the commandments are not merely to be known?
answers: The phrase "before you"
The phrase "observe to do"
The phrase "this day"
questions.explanation: "Observe to do" requires not only knowing or remembering but also putting the commandments into practice.

questions.question: What does the word "all" show about the scope of the command?
answers: It applies only to the judgments
It applies only to the easier laws
It includes every statute and judgment
questions.explanation: The word "all" makes clear that none of the instructions is excluded.
